title: Overview
description: A guide to chan: from your first terminal to remote devservers, gateways, and agent teams.

title: Install & first run
description: Install chan, make it your default terminal, file browser or Markdown editor on Linux, open the Computers screen, and turn a directory into a workspace.

title: Navigation
description: Arrange windows, panes, and tabs, and find actions with the command launcher.

title: Devserver
description: Set up a devserver and connect to its terminals and workspaces from the Computers window.

title: systemd integration
description: Run the devserver as a systemd user service, restart and upgrade it without losing terminals, and report its metrics to systemd-report.

title: Chan in a browser
description: Serve a workspace or a devserver from the chan binary alone and use it from any browser, no desktop needed.

title: Host a gateway
description: Run your own gateway on one server and publish devservers behind sign-in, for you and the people you share them with.

title: Terminal & teams
description: Use terminal commands, rich prompts, drafts, program status, and agent teams.

title: Editor & previews
description: Edit text, preview Markdown, slide decks, and JSON, and export documents to PDF.

title: File browser & reports
description: Browse files, transfer them between machines, and inspect code reports and COCOMO estimates.

title: Graph
description: Navigate directories and relationships, and use depth to see more of a repository.

title: Dashboard & index
description: Read workspace information, follow indexing progress, and manage what gets indexed.

title: Workspace search
description: Find content, files, tags, and relationships through the search UI and terminal.

title: Collaboration & sessions
description: Share workspace sessions, identify clients, and hand over leadership locally or remotely.

title: Extensions
description: Add your own applications as sandboxed tabs and integrate them through the host bridge and cs.

title: Settings & defaults
description: Configure appearance, editing, terminals, shortcuts, and workspace preferences.

title: Screensavers
description: Configure idle locking and explore the animations shown in an empty workspace.
